subject: Cost and Management Accounting
question_html: Employee (labour) cost, as defined in the Study Material, is best described as-

options.A: Benefits paid or payable only to permanent employees for services rendered, in cash only
options.B: Benefits paid or payable to employees, whether permanent or temporary, for services rendered, including payments made in cash and in kind
options.C: Only the monetary wages paid to workers who are directly engaged in the production process
options.D: All payments made to employees, excluding the employer's contribution to statutory welfare funds

answer_html:
Answer: (B) Benefits paid or payable to employees, whether permanent or temporary, for services rendered, including payments made in cash and in kind.

Employee cost is the benefit paid or payable to employees of an entity, whether permanent or temporary, for the services rendered by them, and it includes payments made in cash as well as in kind.

subject: Cost and Management Accounting
question_html: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes direct employee cost from indirect employee cost?

options.A: Direct employee cost is apportioned on a suitable basis while indirect employee cost is allocated to cost units
options.B: Direct employee cost varies with the volume of production, whereas indirect employee cost may not vary with the volume of production
options.C: Direct employee cost is always larger in amount than indirect employee cost in a manufacturing entity
options.D: Indirect employee cost relates only to employees working in the personnel department

answer_html:
Answer: (B) Direct employee cost varies with the volume of production, whereas indirect employee cost may not vary with the volume of production.

Direct employee cost is easily identified and allocated to cost units and has a positive relationship with volume; indirect employee cost is apportioned on some appropriate basis and may not vary with volume.

subject: Cost and Management Accounting
question_html: The essential test for classifying an employee cost as a direct employee cost is that it-

options.C: is paid on a piece-rate basis rather than on a time basis
options.D: forms part of gross wages before statutory deductions are made

answer_html:
Answer: (B) can be attributed to a cost object in an economically feasible manner.

Direct employee cost is the benefit paid or payable to employees which can be attributed to a cost object in an economically feasible manner and thus easily identified with an activity, contract, cost centre, process or product.

question_html: Control over employee cost implies that-

subject: Cost and Management Accounting
question_html: 'M', an employee, gets basic pay of ₹12,000 p.m., dearness allowance of ₹3,000 p.m., bonus at 20% of salary and D.A., other allowances of ₹1,500 p.m., and the employer contributes 10% of salary and D.A. to the provident fund. 'M' works 2,400 hours per annum, of which 300 hours are non-productive and treated as normal idle time. The effective hourly cost of employee 'M' is-
answer_html:
Answer: (D) ₹120.00.

Monthly earnings = ₹12,000 + ₹3,000 + ₹3,000 bonus + ₹1,500 PF + ₹1,500 other allowances = ₹21,000; annual = ₹2,52,000. Effective hours = 2,400 - 300 = 2,100. Effective hourly cost = ₹2,52,000 / 2,100 = ₹120.00. Option (B) wrongly divides by 2,400 hours and option (C) omits the employer's provident fund contribution.

subject: Cost and Management Accounting
question_html: In a factory working six days a week and eight hours each day, a worker is paid ₹110 per day basic plus D.A. at 120% of basic. He is allowed 30 minutes off for a meal break and a 10 minutes recess for rest during each shift. During a week his card showed time chargeable to Job P 16 hours, Job Q 14 hours and Job R 10 hours, the balance being time wasted while waiting for a job. The amount to be charged to the Costing Profit and Loss Account for the week is-

options.A: Nil, as waiting for a job is normal idle time absorbed through the job rates

answer_html:
Answer: (C) ₹132.00.

Effective hours per week = [8 hours - (30 + 10 minutes)] x 6 days = 44 hours. Total weekly wages = (₹110 + 120% of ₹110) x 6 = ₹1,452. Wage rate per hour = ₹1,452 / 44 = ₹33. Time booked to jobs = 16 + 14 + 10 = 40 hours, so waiting time (abnormal idle time) = 44 - 40 = 4 hours, charged at 4 x ₹33 = ₹132.
topic_text: Allocation of weekly wages and abnormal idle time

answer_html:
Answer: (B) the time saved bears to the standard (allowed) time.

question_html: Under the Rowan Plan, the bonus earned by a worker is at its maximum when the time taken is-

options.B: one-third of the time allowed
options.C: one-half of the time allowed
options.D: three-fourths of the time allowed

answer_html:
Answer: (C) one-half of the time allowed.

The bonus under the Rowan Scheme is maximum when the time taken by a worker on a job is half of the time allowed. Beyond that point the bonus actually falls, which is why a worker cannot increase his earnings merely by increasing work speed.

question_html: The bonus paid under the Halsey Plan with bonus at 50% for the time saved will equal the bonus paid under the Rowan System when the actual time taken is-

options.C: 75% of the time allowed
options.D: 25% of the time allowed

answer_html:
Answer: (B) 50% of the time allowed.

Halsey bonus = (50/100) x (SH - AH) x R and Rowan bonus = (AH / SH) x (SH - AH) x R. These are equal when 50/100 = AH / SH, that is, when the actual time taken is 50% of the time allowed.

question_html: If the time saved is less than 50% of the standard time, then a comparison of the wages under the Rowan and Halsey premium plans gives-

Answer: (A) more wages to the worker under the Rowan plan than the Halsey plan.

Answer: (B) ₹17.28.

Time saved = 60 - 48 = 12 hours. Wages = (48 x ₹0.30) + (12/60) x 48 x ₹0.30 = ₹14.40 + ₹2.88 = ₹17.28. Option (A) is the amount under the Halsey Plan and option (D) is the basic time wage without bonus.

subject: Cost and Management Accounting
question_html: A skilled worker is paid a guaranteed wage rate of ₹40 per hour and the standard time for one unit of a product is 5 hours. Under the Rowan Incentive Plan he earned an effective hourly rate of ₹48 on the manufacture of that product. The time actually taken by him was-

options.A: 3.00 hours
options.B: 3.50 hours
options.C: 4.00 hours
options.D: 4.50 hours

answer_html:
Answer: (C) 4.00 hours.

Effective hourly rate under Rowan = Rate + (Time saved / Time allowed) x Rate. Thus ₹48 = ₹40 + [(5 - T)/5] x ₹40, giving (5 - T)/5 = 0.2 and T = 4 hours. Check: earnings = (4 x ₹40) + (1/5 x 4 x ₹40) = ₹192, and ₹192 / 4 hours = ₹48.

subject: Cost and Management Accounting
question_html: The Rowan Plan is said to provide a safeguard against loose fixation of standards by the rate-setting department because-

options.A: the guaranteed day rate is withdrawn if the standards are later found to be loose
options.B: even where a large amount of time is saved, the bonus actually paid remains relatively low

options.D: the standard time is automatically revised whenever the time saved exceeds 50%

answer_html:
Answer: (B) even where a large amount of time is saved, the bonus actually paid remains relatively low.

In the Rowan Scheme the bonus paid will be low where standards are loosely fixed. question_html: A factory with the latest sophisticated machines wants an incentive scheme under which (i) the entire gains of improved production should not go to the workers, (ii) quality should not suffer in the name of speed, and (iii) mistakes by a newly established rate-setting department should not unduly benefit workers. subject: Cost and Management Accounting
question_html: A worker is paid ₹12,000 per month and dearness allowance of ₹3,000 p.m. The worker's contribution to provident fund is 10% and the employer contributes the same amount. The ESIC premium is 6.5% of wages, of which 1.75% is paid by the employee. The firm pays 2 months' wages as bonus each year. The number of working days in a year is 300 of 8 hours each, out of which the worker is entitled to 20 days leave on full pay. The wage rate per hour for costing purposes is-
answer_html:
Answer: (C) ₹105.60.

Annual wages = (₹12,000 + ₹3,000) x 12 = ₹1,80,000; add employer's PF at 10% = ₹18,000; employer's ESI at 4.75% (6.5 - 1.75) = ₹8,550; bonus of 2 months' wages = ₹30,000. Total = ₹2,36,550. Effective hours = (300 - 20) x 8 = 2,240. Rate = ₹2,36,550 / 2,240 = ₹105.60. Option (D) wrongly charges the full 6.5% ESI to the employer and option (B) ignores the leave days.

question_html: Calculate the employee hour rate of worker X from the following data: basic pay ₹15,000 p.m., D.A. ₹4,000 p.m., fringe benefits ₹1,000 p.m. The number of working days in a year is 300, of which 25 days are availed of as holidays on full pay. Assume a day of 8 hours.
